'''Milton Thomas William Hearn''' (born 17 February 1943) is a [[Professor]] of [[Chemistry]] and the Director of the Australian Research Council Special Research Centre for [[Green chemistry|Green Chemistry]] at the [[Monash University]]. He was previously the head of the department of [[Biochemistry]] and [[Molecular Biology]]. His work focuses on studying biomolecular structure, the study of separation science, and using that knowledge to develop green processes. He earned his B.S, [[Ph.D]], and [[D.Sc]] in [[Organic Chemistry]] at [[University of Adelaide]]. He then did his postdoctoral work in Canada before working in New Zealand. From 1981 to 1985, he was a Research Fellow at the [[St. Vincent's Institute of Medical Research]] before joining Monash in 1986. Since 2002, he has been the Director of the Green Chemistry Center.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Briddell|title=Profile - Dr. Milton Hearn|url=https://communities.acs.org/community/science/sustainability/green-chemistry-nexus-blog/blog/2013/01/16/profile--dr-milton-hearn|website=ACS|date=16 January 2013 |accessdate=4 August 2015}}</ref><ref name=LCGC>{{cite web|title=Finalist Dr. Milton Hearn|url=http://images.alfresco.advanstar.com/alfresco_images/pharma/2014/08/21/fda6cb60-754c-44df-be03-9a59a87340cf/article-648563.pdf|website=LCGC|publisher=LCGC|accessdate=4 August 2015}}</ref>

Hearn has received the Leighton Memorial Award from the Royal Australian Chemical Society, the Centennial Medal of the Commonwealth of Australia and the [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Chromatography.<ref>{{cite news|title=Professor wins prestigious American Chemical Society Award in Chromatography|url=http://monash.edu/news/releases/show/professor-wins-prestigious-american-chemical-society-award-in-chromatography|accessdate=4 August 2015|publisher=Monash University|date=20 August 2014}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Victoria]], the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering, the [[Australian Institute of Company Directors]], the Royal Chemical Institute, and [[IUPAC]].<ref name=LCGC /> He was appointed a [[Order of Australia|Member of the Order of Australia]] in the [[2015 Australia Day Honours]] for service to science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Milton Thomas HEARN |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1150844 |access-date=2024-10-10 |website=Australian Honours Search Facility}}</ref>
